en_summary: The Justice Department is investigating whether companies tied to Alice Huang, the woman at the center of the Nvidia scandal, helped smuggle Super Micro $SMCI products into China,
text:
The Justice Department is investigating whether companies tied to Alice Huang, the woman at the center of the Nvidia scandal, helped smuggle Super Micro $SMCI products into China, per Bloomberg.

The probe is being led by the US attorney’s office in Manhattan. It’s unclear whether it’s connected to existing chip-smuggling cases.

Manhattan prosecutors already charged Super Micro co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw and two others in March. They’re accused of conspiring to ship Nvidia-powered servers to a Southeast Asian company and divert them to Chinese customers. Liaw has pleaded not guilty and left the company. Super Micro itself isn’t a defendant and says it’s cooperating.

The DOJ is separately investigating Megaspeed International, Huang’s former company, over suspected chip smuggling. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing.

Penguin just launched its AI Platform Operations Services, targeting neoclouds and enterprises operating large-scale AI infrastructure.

The offering provides end-to-end management of AI factories, including 24/7 monitoring, GPU cluster optimization, incident response, and infrastructure lifecycle management. It’s backed by over 4.2 billion hours of GPU runtime experience.

As AI infrastructure scales, simply deploying GPUs isn’t enough. Neoclouds need to maximize GPU utilization, minimize downtime, and meet increasingly demanding customer SLAs.

This is where I believe Penguin has a significant opportunity.

Rather than just designing and deploying AI infrastructure, $PENG is positioning itself to operate and optimize these AI factories throughout their lifecycle.

That creates the potential for recurring service revenue, deeper customer relationships, and a larger share of AI infrastructure spending.

text:
Why did $BTC fall after the election?

Mark Yusko says margin calls on 2x and 4x leveraged ETFs likely pushed traders to sell gold and Bitcoin, while bonds got a little bid as rates fell

"If you're levered long, and the problem is they're not just levered long, they're in these 2x and 4x levered long ETFs and single-stock ETFs. 4 times levered on a 60-vol asset? Bad plan, bad plan."

"When you get a margin call, and there were lots of margin calls right after the election, what do you sell? Well, you can't sell what just went down, so you sell what you can sell: gold, Bitcoin, bonds."

"Bonds did the opposite. They had the Economist cover curse. The Economist literally, the day of the highest rate, said bonds are dead, and rates have gone down ever since. So bonds actually got a little bid."

"So really, you got gold and Bitcoin to be sold to fund your margin call. And that's exactly what I think happened."

$NBIS - our updated valuation after Q3

Nebius traded near $123 before the open after Q3. We cut revenue per active MW in our capacity model by about 10%, in line with peers like CoreWeave ($9–11m per MW).

Weighted value: ~$220 a share

Base: $271 (was $302)
• 1,750 MW active by end-2027 at $10.8m per MW
• FY2027 revenue of $12.4bn, inside the new $12–13bn outlook
• $6.3bn of FY2027 EBITDA at 16x; ~$4.1bn of equity raised through 2028

Bull: $343 (was $380)
• 2,100 MW, $15.6bn of revenue, and prepayments cover the build with no new equity

Bear: $54 (was $63)
• 1,300 MW and $8.1m per MW, so revenue lands at $7.8bn
• ~$17.5bn of equity raised at $95. Dilution, not EBITDA, drives this case.

What matters most
- Activation pace: every 250 MW is about $3bn of ARR
- Revenue per MW: new contracts at $20–25m per MW leave room above our base case
- Funding: $17–20bn of guided prepayments plus a new $3.5bn Citi facility
- Risk: capex guidance of ~$27bn for 2026 and $40–45bn for 2027 is above what our model assumes.

At ~$123, the market is pricing our bear case’s funding stress, not the base case’s operating path.
